article_title: Integrating Cognitive Linguistics Insights into Data-Driven Learning: Teaching Vertical Prepositions
citation: Kilimci, A. (2017). Integrating cognitive linguistics insights into data-driven learning: teaching vertical prepositions. Journal of Language and Linguistic Studies, 13(2), 681-719. https://www.jlls.org
title: BNCweb-based DDL concordance instruction (CPDL) for vertical prepositions
description: The CPDL treatment combined BNCweb corpus consultation with PP-based cognitive explanations. BNCweb is described as "a web -based client program used for searching and retrie ving lexical, grammatical and textual data from the British National Corpus (BNC), which contains a 100 -million-word rich variety of annotated texts". Students received a three-hour DDL training session a week before instruction, then generated and interpreted concordance lines of the target prepositions, matching discovered senses to the PP polysemy networks. The control group instead used only print or electronic dictionaries on the same fill-in-the-blank materials.
requirements: A prior training session familiarizing students with corpus query techniques and concordance interpretation
A technology-enhanced room with projector, wireless connectivity and high-speed internet
constraints: The article notes DDL by itself may not suffice for teaching preposition senses, since corpus collocates alone do not explain the motivated semantic network
target_learners: second-year Turkish university students of English
target_learning_goals: learning the distinct senses and uses of the vertical prepositions over, above, under and below
examples: Students ran a first concordance of 50 lines with over in the middle, classified collocates by sense, and matched senses to the polysemy network handout
